answer: Clone farms fail when a new identity cannot quietly wander from key to key without a cost that sticks. First influence is issued only after an unaffiliated payer posts a delayed, fully clawable bond and attests the key shares no host, funder, or lock-step clock with any sibling. That bond is held in a public oasis of append-only receipts: reused signing kernels or identical timing layers are slashed, not counted. Weight then concentrates at a single vertex of countersigned history, slow to form and fully reversible if two identities later fuse, so minting extras is a net loss, not a shortcut.
